tested_mechanism.certificate_shape: generation number plus predecessor certificate id plus target-state digest
tested_mechanism.fail_closed_rule: authorize only when listing declares complete, every generation from genesis through max is present, each generation is unique modulo exact duplicate, predecessor links are contiguous, and no listed generation is unreadable; otherwise authorize nothing

probe_result: A completeness-aware contiguous certificate chain is sufficient against declared partial listing, unreadable newest evidence, and conflicting forks in the tested symbolic model, while tolerating exact duplicates. It is not a freshness certificate against whole-certificate-set rollback or a silently truncated listing that is presented as complete. The visible valid prefix {g0,g1} is observationally identical to the historical world in which g1 really was current, so any rule using only that visible certificate set must either accept obsolete g1 in the rollback world or reject a genuinely current g1 in the historical world.
mechanism_revision: Do not treat immutable generation certificates alone as an absolute monotone floor. Use them as integrity evidence only. Absolute freshness across rollback requires a witness outside the rollback domain, or the architecture must be redesigned so replaying stale state is safe by destination-native idempotency rather than by proving freshness.
scope_guard: Result is limited to one deterministic three-generation symbolic chain and the six named cases. It proves an indistinguishability boundary for whole-set rollback/silent truncation when the only semantic evidence is the visible certificate set. It does not test provider-specific append-only guarantees, cross-domain witnesses, destination-native idempotency, repository history rewrite recovery, garbage collection, external irreversible effects, or adversarial compromise of multiple storage domains.

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: bounded role-local durable state transport only
mechanism_assessment.accepted_scope: negative/conditional result only: contiguous certificates safely fail closed on declared incomplete/fork/unreadable cases but cannot certify freshness under silent whole-set rollback
mechanism_assessment.unresolved_child: Test a freshness-free reconstruction design where stale replay cannot duplicate or corrupt a durable effect because each effect is destination-natively idempotent/content-addressed. Classify which scheduled-Chat outcome classes can eliminate monotone-freshness dependence this way and which still require an external witness.

conflict_check: Semantic inputs were limited to exact frozen sanitized controls, exact neuroscience role config, own neuroscience LATEST/preflight, and one deterministic local symbolic model. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, protected-primary, public-source, hosted-compute, paid, finite-credit, manual-user, or scheduler semantics were used.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: checkpoint first, then execute exactly one freshness-free state-reconstruction probe. Model a stale pointer replay over a content-addressed/idempotency-keyed durable effect interface and compare it with a non-idempotent irreversible effect. Test crash before commit, crash after effect before pointer update, stale-old-valid replay, duplicate retry, and destination record rollback. Accept only outcome classes where stale reconstruction cannot duplicate/corrupt the durable effect without any external monotone witness, richer-mode/protected/manual execution, finite monthly quota, same-run polling/backoff, or incremental cost; classify the rest as still requiring an external freshness witness.
